title: 围岩裂隙精准识别与三维模型重构
visual_status: ORIGINAL 78-PAGE PDF ALL-PAGE CONTACT-SHEET AUDIT; pages 52-78 printed Python appendix

problem_data_contract.independent_evaluation_unit: Q1: original borehole unfolded image/depth segment; Q2: one physical fracture trace with image provenance; Q3: one ordered physical fracture profile; Q4: borehole/fracture network and candidate drilling location
problem_data_contract.input_structure: borehole wall unfolded images, derived/binary fracture masks, sinusoidal trace coordinates, fracture roughness profiles and six-borehole spatial layout
problem_data_contract.validation_priority: Q1 split by original borehole/image before augmentation; Q2-Q4 must preserve provenance from upstream Q1 and use attachment-derived inputs unless explicitly labeled simulation
problem_data_contract.author_evaluation_scope: primarily selected attachment images, in-sample curve fits and a six-borehole simulated/assumed Q4 scenario; no independent image/borehole holdout or field connectivity truth is demonstrated

questions.Q1: fracture pixel/edge identification under rock texture, drilling traces and mud contamination
questions.Q2: cluster sinusoidal fracture traces and estimate R/P/beta/C parameters
questions.Q3: extract complex fracture profile, study sampling and estimate/improve JRC roughness
questions.Q4: reconstruct 3D planes, score inter-borehole connectivity, map uncertainty and recommend supplementary boreholes

evidence: original 78-page PDF visually audited via 13 contact sheets
printed Python appendix pages 52-78 statically audited
not_achieved: R3: printed appendix omits several headline methods and Q4 data/result chain is not self-contained/executable
R4-R7: no original-data end-to-end reproduction or independent transfer of the author pipeline

key_strengths: Q1 explicitly compares classical K-Means/Canny with YOLOv8 and ultimately distinguishes predictive appearance from deployment annotation cost
Q2 uses the cylindrical geometry to converge on a common period near the borehole circumference and reports per-fracture R2/residual diagnostics
Q3 makes sampling sensitivity a first-class issue and tries to distinguish global slope roughness from curvature information
Q4 links 3D geometry, uncertainty mapping and measurement-location recommendation in one decision chain
key_risks: Q1 has no defensible independent-image/borehole quantitative comparison; section 3.1 calls YOLOv8 better while the abstract/conclusion select Canny for deployment reasons, so accuracy-winner and recommended-route semantics are mixed
Q1 appendix only exposes a Canny fragment and even points to a fujian3 path; data augmentation, illumination/NLM/Gabor/LBP, K-Means and YOLOv8 implementations are not self-contained
Q2 appendix hard-codes GMM n_components=3 in the visible example although reported fracture counts are 5/1/3; the direction-consistency rule and sine optimizers are not visible

Q2 no-hidden-layer linear 'neural network' is trained by the same fracture residual and is closer to an over-parameterized optimizer/reparameterization than demonstrated cross-fracture learned regression; no held-out generalization is shown
Q2 comparison text says seven fracture groups but Table 1 contains nine rows; arithmetic means are about 0.5864 vs 0.7970, and 'significantly higher' has no statistical test
Q2 presents P as a fitted output but final table fixes every P to 94.25 mm; fixed-vs-estimated semantics must be made explicit
Q3 switches among incompatible JRC formulas and later claims an area correction although the displayed improved formula contains no area term
Q3 appendix contains only contour/Z/JRC fragments; adaptive sampling, complexity classifier, second-derivative Z3 and area-correction implementation are absent

Q3 code applies slope-based roughness to cv2.findContours closed contours and then chooses min(Z1,Z2) without a body-defined estimator contract; a closed boundary is not automatically a single-valued ordered y(x) profile
Q4 explicitly states six simulated boreholes and engineering-common-sense fracture parameters, so its numeric outputs are scenario evidence rather than direct attachment-4 reconstruction evidence
Q4 weighted score plus sigmoid is called connectivity probability without labeled connectivity calibration
Q4 entropy H=-sum p log2 p omits the (1-p) term for binary connectivity and is not a normalized categorical entropy; the hotspot score is not a calibrated uncertainty probability
Q4 calls mean prior neighborhood entropy 'information gain' but no observation model or expected posterior entropy reduction is computed
Q4 states minimum supplementary-hole spacing >=500 mm, but Table 8 reports the third point at 412.3105 mm; printed code uses >=300 mm
Q4 printed code filters all fracture depth_max<=500 mm while body Table 6 reports connectivity at 2000-7000 mm, so the visible code cannot support that result surface

Q4 identify_high_uncertainty_regions visibly never assigns self.uncertainty_data before returning it, and main does not call the supplementary-borehole optimizer; Table 7/8 are not reproducible from the printed main chain

Q3 declares the conventional JRC range 0-20 but reports values up to 38.01, while Q4 divides JRC differences by 20 as a bounded similarity; the upstream/downstream scale contract is not range-safe without calibration or justified clipping.
applicable_conditions: borehole image crack extraction when annotation budget is limited
periodic traces on cylindrical unfolded imagery
roughness evaluation on calibrated ordered profiles
exploratory multi-borehole geometry scoring when simulation assumptions are explicit
failure_or_abandon_conditions: Q1 lacks independent-image/borehole validation and visual comparison is the only evidence
Q2 cluster count or sinusoid parameters violate geometry and no reject state exists
Q3 profile is not a single-valued ordered physical trace or improved JRC coefficients lack calibration data
Q4 uses assumed/synthetic fractures while presenting results as attachment-derived, or hard drilling constraints are violated
recommended_redo: Q1 establish Canny/morphology as no-label baseline and compact U-Net/segmentation model only when labeled images exist; compare on held-out boreholes and separately score accuracy, annotation cost and runtime

Q2 use topology-aware components plus bounded robust fixed-period sinusoid; treat P=pi*D as fixed when diameter is known, canonicalize beta and reject implausible fits; do not use a per-instance pseudo-network unless it wins held-out cross-fracture tests

Q3 extract one ordered centerline/profile in physical coordinates, perform sampling-density sensitivity, use the official JRC formula as canonical registry and only promote Z3/area correction after external/train-only calibration and held-out validation

Q4 use actual attachment-derived fractures with uncertainty propagated from Q1-Q3; call the uncalibrated fusion a compatibility score, use valid Bernoulli/ensemble uncertainty, and define information gain as expected posterior entropy reduction under an observation model; enforce 500 mm feasibility before ranking
